b001.text: In a safe house in Virginia, a young Ukrainian hacker is typing.

b002.text: The room is wired, every chat monitored, every word logged.

b003.text: An agent watches from the doorway.

b004.text: On paper, Maksym Popov is cooperating.

b005.text: He is telling the FBI what it wants to hear.

b006.text: And in the same messages, in street Russian nobody in the building speaks, he is telling his crew exactly where he is, and who has him.

b007.text: It will take the Bureau three months to translate what he wrote in front of them.

b008.text: By then, the pattern of the coming decade is already set.

b009.text: This is the man the FBI will use to take down one of the largest stolen-card forums on earth.

b010.text: He will do it from a jail cell, chained to a desk.

b011.text: He will become the asset the Bureau cannot replace, and the reason an agent's career ends with a badge laid on a desk.

b012.text: And years later, he will tell a journalist that the Bureau paid him ten thousand dollars to solve a crime: his own.

b013.text: None of that has happened yet.

b014.text: Right now, there is only the typing, and the watchers who cannot read it.

b015.text: What do you do with a prisoner who is worth more than his cell?

b016.text: Let's go back, to Zhytomyr, and a modem.
